answer.why: Both Summit Hotel Properties and Park Hotels & Resorts are publicly traded lodging REITs that own branded hotel properties, lease them to taxable REIT subsidiaries, have them operated by third-party managers under major franchise brands (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG), and derive revenue from guest room stays and ancillary hotel services. Both serve US business and leisure travelers. The main distinction is that Summit is concentrated in upscale select-service hotels (Hampton Inn, Courtyard, Residence Inn, Hyatt Place, etc.) while Park is 90%+ luxury/upper upscale with a resort portfolio (Hilton Hawaiian Village, Casa Marina Key West). Despite this tier difference, both operate identical business structures and serve the same broad customer set within the same lodging REIT niche—they are regularly considered peers in the lodging REIT comp universe.
